newsitem.title: USA: Oregon tax measure soundly defeated - officials.
newsitem.headline: Oregon tax measure soundly defeated - officials.

text.p: An Oregon ballot measure that would tighten requirements for tax measure approval was defeated Tuesday, according to state officials.
Measure 46 would alter the debt issuance process in Oregon by redefining the voting majority to "all eligible" voters rather than, as it currently stands, all those who "participate" in a vote.
With 36 percent of precincts reporting, Measure 46 was opposed by 89 percent, with 11 percent in support, state officials said.
Measure 32, which would permit the state to issue lottery revenue bonds for a light rail project, appeared headed for defeat, with 54 percent opposed versus support of 46 percent.

The vote on Measure 47, which would limit property taxes, was still too close to call, with opponents narrowly ahead by about 2,000 votes. State officials said they did not expect to be able to call Measure 47 until Thursday.
